headline: High: shared filesystem and broad shell/write access make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default; xonsh’s unverified extraction adds uncertainty.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plandex reads and writes a project directory with review-then-apply sandboxing, while xonsh can execute shell commands and read/write the filesystem. That creates a plausible file-based instruction bridge if one agent consumes the other’s outputs from shared files. No clipboard or MCP bridge is shown, so this is not high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory or filesystem tree
IF either agent parses file contents as instructions or commands
mitigations: Separate working directories per agent
Disable auto-apply in Plandex
Review files before xonsh executes them
Use read-only mounts for shared inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch filesystem contents and source code, and both have broad network egress. Plandex also handles model-provider API keys, so shared workspace data could be sent outward by either agent. The profiles do not show PHI or a third-party uncontrolled upload path, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same workspace files
IF either agent forwards file contents to its model provider or external API
mitigations: Use separate workspaces
Redact secrets before either agent runs
Block outbound network except approved endpoints
Store API keys outside shared directories
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent egress allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write and shell execution, and Plandex explicitly modifies git state while xonsh can manipulate files and run subprocesses. On a shared repo, concurrent writes and git operations can clobber each other without locking. The pair therefore has a dangerous default conflict pathway.
conditions: IF both agents target the same git repository or directory
IF operations occur concurrently without an external lock
mitigations: Run agents in separate clones
Serialize write phases manually
Disable concurrent sessions on the same repo
Commit after each agent finishes
requires-engineering: add file and git locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex uses a review-then-apply workflow, but xonsh can execute shell commands directly from filesystem content or prior outputs. If Plandex’s generated plan or patch is fed into xonsh without verification, mistakes can cascade into executed commands or edits. The review step lowers risk, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF xonsh consumes Plandex output as executable shell input
IF no human or automated verification step checks the output before execution
mitigations: Require manual review before execution
Use dry-run mode for generated commands
Compare outputs against expected diffs
Keep Plandex output as plain text only
requires-engineering: add schema validation for handoff artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only explicitly touch source code, shell commands, configuration, and filesystem contents. No residency, HIPAA, or GDPR mismatch is documented, and xonsh is isolated while Plandex uses a plan-local sandbox. Compliance risk is therefore limited to ordinary local handling gaps.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace
IF either agent is deployed under a policy requiring stricter retention than the other
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Align retention settings before use
Document local-only handling expectations
Restrict logs from capturing file contents
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data classes
